correctness.rationale: For all prime powers q and all nondegenerate binary symmetric B, ring coordinates F_q+V+F_q z are canonical under the assumptions. At a nonzero socle target the product matrix decomposes as q-1 disjoint K_{1,q^3} stars, one isolated vertex, and C tensor J_q with C(v,w)=1[B(v,w)=c]. Direct solution counting gives C^2 entries q on diagonal, zero off diagonal within projective lines, one between distinct lines. The projective perpendicular involution has t fixed lines. The line-constant subspace supplies q once, +1 (q+1-t)/2, -1 (q-1+t)/2; its orthocomplement has C^2=qI and trace zero, giving equal +/-sqrt(q) multiplicity (q+1)(q-2)/2. Scaling by q and adding star eigenvalues proves the full polynomial and rank. Independently constructed matrices match over q=2,3,4, and incidence checks match q=5. Numerical checks are supporting tests only.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected motivating arXiv:2601.19301v1 defines Au(R) but Theorem 3.1 concerns unit targets, Theorems 4.1, 4.4, 4.7 assume J^(n-1) nonzero for ring size q^n (hence J^3 nonzero at n=4), and Theorem 5.1 assumes J^2=0. The present rings satisfy J^2 nonzero and J^3=0, with nonzero socle targets. Neither a specialization nor a corollary of those theorem statements. Searches for the same all-field, all-Witt-type product-matrix classification and possible bilinear-incidence equivalences found no coverage; unindexed historical versions remain a qualification.

value.rationale: The nonzero-socle product matrix is a natural product-equation invariant of local rings. The theorem completely resolves a substantial intermediate-radical case excluded by the motivating maximal/minimal-nilpotency theorems, uniformly in all finite characteristics and all binary Gorenstein Witt types. It proves that signed q-eigenvalue multiplicities reconstruct the underlying isotropic-line type: a structural ring-theoretic recovery statement, not simply numerical enumeration.
